AKM Foiz, Advocate instructed by Md. Sajjadul Huq, Advocate-on-Record — For the Appellant. 
Shamsul Alam, Advocate instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record — For the Respondents.
parties:
Ali Akkas  ----- Appellant
Vs.
Enayet Hossain and others  ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J: This appeal at the instance of the informant-appellant (father) directed against the Judgment and order dated 4-4-96 passed by the Division Bench of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.2448 of 1995 thereby quashing the proceedings of GR Case No.683/94 pending in the court of Thana Magistrate Munshiganj under sections 366A/34 of the Penal Code. 

 2. The appellant lodged an FIR on 25-9-94 against accused-respondent Nos.1-5 alleging that his minor daughter Ruma Akhter aged about 11 years was kidnapped by the said respondents in collusion with each other while she was on her way back from school on 14-9-94 and that she was being wrongfully confined in an unknown place with dishonest intention. On these above allegations police investigated into the case and submitted charge-sheet against the respondents on 31-12-94 under sections 366A/ 109 of the Penal Code. 

 3. Subsequent thereto the accused-respondents appeared before the learned Magistrate and they were enlarged on bail. Two of the accused absconded and warrant of arrest was issued against them after accepting the charge-sheet by the learned Magistrate. At that stage, the accused respondents filed an application for quashing before the High Court Division and a Rule was issued on 6-8-95 and all further proceedings of the aforesaid case was stayed. 

 5. Leave was granted to consider whether the learned Judges of the High Court Division illegally quashed the proceedings of GR Case No 683 of 1994 of the Court of Thana Magistrate, Munshiganj, occasioning a serious miscarriage of justice, contrary to the principles enunciated by this Division in the case of Abdul Quader Chowdhury and others vs. State reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38 and in the case of Bangladesh vs. Tan Kheng Hock reported in 31 DLR (AD) 69, and whether the learned Judges by the impugned judgment has stifled the trial upon pre-judging the matter on the basis of an alleged statement of a minor girl causing an abuse of the inherent jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 6. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that in deciding the Rule for quashing, the learned Judges considered a part of the charge-sheet and the statement of the victim girl recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and observed that there was no case of kidnapping and the accused had no connection with the incident of leaving the parents house by Ruma Akhter. Victim girl Ruma Akhter made a statement under section 164 of the Code before a Magistrate on 26-9-94 when she was produced by accused Enayet Hossain. In her statement the victim girl stated that she read in Class VI in Esapura High School and that she went 12/13 days ago to the house of Giasuddin, grand-father at Mirpur, Dhaka. From there she went to Kalyanpur alone at her own will. Nobody abducted or kidnapped her and she stayed there and accused Enayet Hossain brought her to Serajdee Khan Police-Station and she went to Dhaka on her own accord. In a later part of the charge-sheet it is stated that accused Enayet Hossain brought the victim to the police station after giving her threats that she will not disclose the real occurrence. In other words, the charge- sheet itself reveals that the aforesaid statement under section 164 CrPc was made under threat and intimidation. In deciding the case, the learned Judges in fact acted wrongly and illegally in relying upon a part of the charge-sheet and the statement of victim girl as indicated above. 

 7. It is also surprising to note that the learned Judges after finding that the allegations made in the First Information Report do constitute an offence most illegally and wrongly quashed the proceeding for securing the ends of justice and also to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court. In the quashing proceeding, the High Court Division is only to see whether there are materials on record to show that the allegations made in the First Information Report and the charge-sheet do in fact constitute an offence and not beyond that. The trial Court will decide the case on the basis of the evidence which will be adduced in the case. The High Court Division cannot at this stage perform the function of a trial Court in quashing the proceeding. The learned Judges of the High Court Division were also wrong in holding that "there is evidence as above which is clearly inconsistent with the accusation. The charge-sheet and other statements which are on record are only materials and the stage of taking evidence has not at all arisen. The observation of the learned Judges that "there is evidence" is absolutely erroneous and uncalled for. In fact, the learned Judges confused evidence with pre-trial materials. 

 8. In the case of Abdul Quader Chowdhury and others vs. State reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38, this Division has clearly spelt out the categories of cases where the High Court Division should interfere to quash a criminal proceeding. In that decision this Division observed as follows: 

 (1) Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on the admitted facts no case can stand against the accused. 

 (3) Where there is a legal bar against institution or continuance of a criminal case against an accused person. 

 (4) In a case where the allegations in the First Information Report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute the offence alleged and in such cases no question of weighing and appreciating evidence arises. 

 (5) The allegations made against the accused person do constitute an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge. This refers to case at a trial stage and thereafter. 

 9. Keeping these settled principles in view it can be said that the learned Judges of the High Court Division most illegally and contrary to the established principles laid down in the said decision of this Division had wrongly interfered with the case and quashed the proceeding of the criminal case. 

 10. For the foregoing reasons, the impugned judgment of the High Court Division is set aside and the proceedings of GR case No 683 of 1994 is restored to its file and number for continuance in accordance with law after setting aside the order of quashing.
